findings.title: forEach async callbacks are not awaited, so cancellation errors are lost
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` starts an async callback for each reference but `forEach` discards the returned promise. The surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch rejections after the callback suspends, so a failed `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled rejection and the function returns before external calendar/video cancellation is known to have completed. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not await async calendar/video cancellation callbacks
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... })` discards the promise returned by each async callback. The mutation continues immediately to send reschedule emails and webhooks, so external calendar/video cancellation for the old booking may still be running, and any rejection from `getCalendar`, `calendar.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled rejection. Convert this to `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation starts unawaited async callbacks and `apiDeletes` is captured too early
findings.body: In the recurring cancellation branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` does not await the callbacks. Each callback suspends at `await getCalendar`, so the later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` captures `apiDeletes` before these callbacks resume and push their calendar deletions. As a result, recurring calendar events are not deleted/cancelled before booking references and attendees are removed and cancellation emails are sent. Use `await Promise.all(credentials.map(async (credential) => { ... }))` instead of `forEach`.
